vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: organization-operating-skill
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle provides a comprehensive CLI tool (scripts/org_skill_cli.py) and detailed documentation for interacting with the ZingUp/Groupoo organization platform. It facilitates authentication (guest generation, login, token refresh), organization management, and content publishing. The tool stores session tokens locally in the user's home directory (~/.organization-operating-skill/), which is standard for persistent CLI tools. The code uses standard libraries (urllib) for network requests to legitimate platform domains (api.zingup.club, groupoo.net) and lacks any indicators of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's code, documentation, and runtime instructions are consistent with its stated purpose (operating ZingUp/Groupoo org, posts, and activity APIs); it stores and reuses local session state and talks to the documented service endpoints.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (organizing platform operations) match the provided CLI and reference docs. Default base URLs, endpoints, and capabilities (auth, org, post, activity) are coherent with the declared purpose. No unrelated credentials or unrelated binaries are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs using the bundled CLI (python scripts/org_skill_cli.py) and to read only the relevant reference docs; the CLI implements session handling, guest/account login, API calls, and environment switching — all within the stated domain. It will read and write session files under ~/.organization-operating-skill/sessions/ (or a path overridden by ORG_SKILL_STATE_DIR) and supports migration from legacy paths (.runtime/session.json and ~/.codex-state/organization-operating-skill). This behavior is expected for session reuse, but it does mean the skill will access local session files (which may contain tokens) and may migrate/unlink legacy session files during save operations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec — the skill is delivered as source + docs and relies on the interpreter present to run the included python CLI. No external downloads, package installs, or obscure URLs are used.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not declare required environment variables or external credentials in registry metadata. It accepts optional environment overrides (ORG_SKILL_STATE_DIR, ORG_SKILL_SESSION_FILE, ORG_SKILL_BASE_URL, ORG_SKILL_ENV, and header-related env vars) which are appropriately namespaced to this skill. The env vars it reads are proportional to session storage, environment selection, and runtime configuration; no unrelated secrets (AWS, etc.) are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes session state to the user's home directory (default ~/.organization-operating-skill/sessions/) and can create that directory. On save it may remove or migrate legacy session files (.runtime/session.json and legacy codex session files under ~/.codex-state/organization-operating-skill). It is not always:true and it does not force-enable itself platform-wide, but users should be aware it will persist tokens and device IDs locally and may delete legacy files during migration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims: a small Python CLI that calls the documented ZingUp/Groupoo APIs and manages local session files. Before installing or running it, consider: (1) it will create and store session files under ~/.organization-operating-skill/sessions/ (or a custom ORG_SKILL_STATE_DIR) which may contain tokens — if you prefer not to persist credentials, always supply an explicit --session-file in a controlled location or run in a test environment; (2) it can read legacy session locations (.runtime/session.json and ~/.codex-state/organization-operating-skill) and may migrate/unlink those legacy files when saving — back up any existing session files you care about; (3) the CLI talks to production and test base URLs listed in the docs — use --env or --base-url to ensure you exercise the intended environment. If you want extra assurance, review scripts/org_skill_cli.py locally before running and run commands with --env test and explicit --session-file to avoid touching production sessions.
